article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Evening Brief
article.dek: The board caught up on the Ravens' quarterback, two lines moved through Friday afternoon, and Sunday's forecast is clear and mild everywhere.

items.headline: Ravens confirm Huntley — and the board caught up
paragraphs: The app now lists Tyler Huntley as Baltimore's expected starter for Sunday at Cleveland. This morning it still showed Lamar Jackson with a Questionable tag — it has caught up to Thursday's news.
The line followed the news: the Ravens moved from -3.5 to -3.0 on DraftKings this afternoon.
items.takeaway: The app is current on the quarterback news now. If you want Baltimore, this morning's -3.5 is gone — tap Check on the -3.0 you can actually get before you decide.

items.headline: Quarterback roundup: all eyes on Sunday inactives
paragraphs: The Eagles show Tanner McKee starting at home against Carolina — Jalen Hurts is out with the calf issue. Tampa Bay shows Jalon Daniels starting with Baker Mayfield out again. Caleb Williams is listed as Chicago's starter Sunday at Atlanta after two full practices.
Everything else on the slate holds: Josh Allen, C.J. Stroud, Patrick Mahomes, Justin Herbert, Jayden Daniels, and Cam Ward all listed as expected starters.
items.takeaway: Facts only, nothing new to bet. Sunday's inactive lists land about 90 minutes before each kickoff — Sunday morning's brief will carry the final designations.

items.headline: Sunday weather: clear and mild, confirmed
paragraphs: The final NWS daytime forecasts for Sunday's outdoor venues: Cleveland sunny and 61, Philadelphia sunny and 57, Foxborough sunny and 51. Winds light everywhere.
Nothing changed through the day. There are no weather games on Sunday's slate.
items.takeaway: Nothing in the forecast changes how you read Sunday's games. File it as clear and move on.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Tonight's three cards, with real numbers
paragraphs: Hit Rate: Bills moneyline -230 on DraftKings at the Raiders. The model gives Buffalo a 71.8% win chance (trust 69.2%), reliability MEDIUM, recommended 0.75 unit. This card picks the supported pick most likely to win — remember the app's own tutorial: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

Balanced: Giants moneyline -104 on FanDuel against the Saints. Model probability 65.3% against a market-implied 50.0% (trust 57.7%), MEDIUM, 0.75 unit. The middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much.
Value: Falcons +1.5 spread -115 on FanDuel against the Bears. The model's plus-EV play at +1.7% EV, MEDIUM, 0.75 unit.
items.takeaway: Three cards, three different jobs. Hit Rate = most likely to win. Balanced = strong without paying too much. Value = the model's plus-EV play. Pick the job that fits your read.

items.headline: Your book doesn't match the card? Tap Check
paragraphs: Lines moved this afternoon — the Ravens and Panthers each a half-point, and the Bills price drifted from -218 to -230. The board refreshes every morning and evening, but your book is your book.
Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override — a bet/no-bet verdict on YOUR price.
items.takeaway: Check turns any price you can actually get into a fresh verdict. Use it before you bet, not after.

items.headline: Learn the Game: the vig
paragraphs: The vig — short for vigorish, also called the juice — is the book's cut baked into every price you see.

Here's a clearly labeled hypothetical. Imagine a game where both sides are listed at -110. You risk $1.10 to win $1.00 — that extra ten cents is the vig. Now imagine you place ten of those $1.10 bets and split them five and five. You've staked $11.00 and you collect $10.00 back. A .500 record, and you're down a dollar.
That's the hill every bettor climbs: at -110 prices you need to win about 52.4% of your bets just to break even.
items.takeaway: The vig is why a 50/50 record still loses money — and why the app's plus-EV check matters more than picking winners. (The example above is hypothetical, not real betting activity.)

items.headline: Ravens -3.5 down to -3.0 with Huntley confirmed
paragraphs: The Ravens dropped a half-point on DraftKings this afternoon, and the app now lists Tyler Huntley as the expected starter — it caught up to Thursday's practice news.
This is a news move with the quarterback confirmation behind it, not mystery money.
items.takeaway: If you want the Ravens, the -3.0 is the number to price — and tap Check on your book's actual line before you do.

items.headline: Panthers -3.5 down to -3.0, Packers price eased
paragraphs: Carolina's line drifted a half-point toward Philadelphia on DraftKings through the day — the Eagles sit +3.0 at -118 odds now. Over in the NFC North, the Packers -1.5 price softened from -115 to -105.
Everything else parked: Chiefs -7.5, Steelers -2.5, Patriots -7.5, 49ers -7.5 all exactly where they were this morning.
items.takeaway: Nothing here to chase. Prices move, the model's read doesn't — until the news says otherwise.

items.headline: The cards moved too: Bills -218 to -230, Falcons -110 to -115
paragraphs: The Hit Rate card's Bills price drifted from -218 this morning to -230 tonight. The Value card's Falcons +1.5 ticked from -110 to -115 on FanDuel. The Balanced card's Giants -104 is unchanged.
Same picks, slightly worse prices than this morning's board.
items.takeaway: Another reason to Check your book's number instead of trusting the card's price from this morning.

items.headline: Tonight's job: lock the plan, not the bets
paragraphs: The board is set for the evening and the big quarterback questions have answers. But lines can still move overnight, and nothing plays until Sunday.
If you've got a lean, write it down. Then re-check Sunday morning's edition before anything is final.
items.takeaway: Plans are free. Bets are final. Keep it that way until Sunday.

items.headline: Sunday's final answers arrive Sunday morning
paragraphs: Inactive lists post about 90 minutes before each kickoff — that's when the Williams and Huntley designations become official.
The morning edition carries the final calls plus a fresh board. Read it before you touch anything.
items.takeaway: No Sunday bet is final until the inactives and the morning board are in. Read Sunday's edition first.
